sections.html: Neptune's gatekeeper is Code Enforcement. A Certificate of Inspection has to be in hand before a buyer can move in, and the checklist backs that rule with fines up to $2,000. The township covers 8.13 square miles of land in Monmouth County, running from the ocean at Ocean Grove to the Garden State Parkway.

Population is about 28,273, close to what it was in 2020. Owners live in 70.2 percent of housing, the midpoint owned-home value is $455,900 and midpoint household income is $101,017. About 20.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, so estate sales and downsizing supply many listings. Midpoint gross rent is $1,876 and the average commute is 26.1 minutes.

Buyers shop by neighborhood. Ocean Grove is a 220-acre Victorian seaside district on the National Register, bounded by Fletcher Lake, Route 71, Lake Wesley and the Atlantic. Shark River Hills sits along the estuary on the south border. Mid-Town is in a township-led revitalization, and West Neptune holds the Route 66 commercial strip. The Gables, Green Grove, Summerfield, Bradley Park and Seaview Island complete the list. Jersey Shore University Medical Center anchors the township's health care sector.

Five state routes (18, 33, 35, 66 and 71) pass through, and Garden State Parkway access comes at Exits 100 and 102. Bradley Beach station on the North Jersey Coast Line takes riders to Newark Penn, Secaucus Junction, New York Penn and Hoboken. NJ Transit buses 317, 830, 832 and 836 serve the township.

Neptune Township Schools run Gables, Green Grove, Midtown Community, Shark River Hills and Summerfield for PreK-5, then Neptune Middle School and Neptune High School.

Selling, buying or renting without the certificate risks a fine up to $2,000 and as many as 90 days in jail. The Transfer of Title application costs $65, is non-refundable, and has the buyer swear not to occupy the home until the certificate is clear, with a fine up to $1,250 otherwise.

Before an inspection is booked, every construction permit and violation must be closed and municipal charges, meaning property taxes and sewer, must be current. An estate needs the surrogate's certificate naming the executor. The application expires after 30 days, and the home must be empty on inspection day.

  • Outside: house numbers at least 3 inches tall, no flaking paint, gutters and downspouts attached, safe railings and walks, and a trash and recycling cart left behind.
  • Inside: smoke detectors on every level, carbon monoxide alarms near bedrooms where required, GFCI outlets in kitchens and baths, and a marked furnace shut-off.
  • Unused oil tanks come out or get filled, which requires a demolition permit.
  • Wood stoves and fireplaces need a certified chimney sweep's letter.

Code Enforcement works from 25 Neptune Boulevard, phone 732-988-5200, extension 260, and the township's forms page takes online applications.

Neptune separates rentals into categories. A standard rental application is for leases of a year (365 days) or longer, and a pre-1978 building needs a lead certificate or lead inspection.

Tenants complicate a sale because the unit must be vacant when the inspector visits. Match move-out dates to your closing date, and ask Code Enforcement whether the buyer needs an owner-occupancy certificate or a rental certificate once the deed is recorded.

Installments are the first of February, May, August and November, each with ten days of grace. Arrears up to $1,500 carry 8% a year and larger balances carry 18%, and a penalty of up to 6% may be added to unpaid balances above $10,000 at year end. Sewer bills come separately, on March 1 and September 1. A municipal charge still open on November 11 can be sold at tax sale.

The Tax Collector cannot adjust an assessment, so errors go to the assessor. Seniors and Social Security disability recipients can apply for property tax relief on the PAS-1 form, and forms for a military service deduction are on the Tax Office page. Call 732-988-5200, extension 251, for the exact payoff.

Recording happens at the Monmouth County Clerk's main office, Market Yard, 33 Mechanic Street, Freehold, where recording runs 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. The clerk's phone is 732-431-7324.

The fee is $40 for a deed's first page and $10 for extra pages, and transfer tax is due when the deed is recorded. A revised fee for sales over $1 million took effect on July 10, 2025 under P.L. 2025, c. 69. Confirm current numbers with your closing attorney.

The inspection step makes a conventional sale slower when a house needs work. As-is buyers suit estate properties, houses with tenants and homes with unfinished permits.

  • Listing: broadest exposure, especially for Ocean Grove and Shark River Hills.
  • Owner sale: you keep the commission and do the paperwork.
  • Cash purchase: no repairs asked, a closing date that fits you, and the inspection still due before anyone moves in.

Subtract inspection costs, the tax payoff and closing costs from each offer, then pick the timeline you prefer.

Work backward from the closing date. The application expires after 30 days, so do not file it too early, but file it soon enough that the inspector has an opening. Before filing, close all permits and pay any open tax or sewer balance, because Code Enforcement will not book the visit without them.

Empty the house before inspection day and leave the trash and recycling cart behind. Test each detector, check the GFCI outlets in the kitchen and baths, and have a chimney sweep's letter ready if there is a fireplace or wood stove. For an estate, bring the surrogate's certificate naming the executor.

Keep every receipt and approval in one folder for the buyer's attorney, including the permit closeouts, the tax and sewer payoff and the chimney letter. If you live far away, ask whether a relative or agent can let the inspector in, since a vacant house is required and a missed appointment only delays the closing and may require a new application.

On closing day the attorney sends the deed to Freehold, and the buyer must wait for a clear certificate before moving in. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, but the township still requires the certificate.

faqs.q: Must a Neptune house have a Certificate of Inspection to be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The township checklist lists fines up to $2,000 and up to 90 days in jail for buying, selling or renting without one, and the Transfer of Title application costs $65.

faqs.q: Can buyers move into a Neptune house before the inspection clears?
faqs.a: No. The Transfer of Title affidavit commits the buyer not to occupy the home until a clear certificate exists, and the form lists a fine up to $1,250 for doing so.

faqs.q: What dates does Neptune use for property tax installments?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November, each followed by ten days of grace. Sewer charges fall due on March 1 and September 1.

faqs.q: Which items does Neptune Code Enforcement look at?
faqs.a: Permits and violations, current taxes and sewer, house numbers, detectors, GFCI outlets, the furnace, stairs, gutters and trash carts, among others. The Certificate of Inspection checklist has the full list.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Neptune deed?
faqs.a: The Monmouth County Clerk at 33 Mechanic Street in Freehold, open for recording on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.
